## Claims
- [source-backed] Section 4 begins “Conclusion of the proof”; it contains Definition 4.1, Lemmas 4.2–4.3, then Theorems 4.4–4.5. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 737-789]
- [source-backed] With valid \(\varphi=(n,r,i,j,a,b,N)\), the source’s equation (8) is
  \[
  \left\{
  \sum_{\substack{\lambda\subseteq b^a\\|\lambda|<N}}
  \sum_{\substack{\theta\subseteq(n-r)^r\\|\theta|=N-|\lambda|}}
  c_{(i^j,\lambda),\theta}^{\nu}A_{\lambda,\theta}
  =\chi(\nu)
  \ \middle|\ 
  \nu\in\operatorname{Dec}_{\varphi}
  \right\},
  \tag{8}
  \]
  where
  \[
  \chi(\nu)=
  \begin{cases}
  f_{\nu_B},&\nu\text{ is tall},\\
  0,&\nu\text{ is wide}.
  \end{cases}
  \]
  Here “valid” means \(n,r,i,j,a,b,N\ge1\), \(r<n\), \(a+j\le r\), \(a+i\le n-r\), \(b\le i,j\), \(N\le ab\); \(\operatorname{Dec}_\varphi\) consists of allowable \(\nu\) with \(\nu_{j+1}\le b\) and \(\ell(\nu)\le j+a\), and “tall” means \(\nu_1=i\), otherwise “wide.” The notation \(\nu_B\) is the component of the source’s Figure-1 decomposition. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 300-340]
- [source-backed] Equation (9), after \(\Delta(s_\nu)=\sum_{\lambda,\mu}c_{\lambda,\mu}^{\nu}(s_\lambda\otimes s_\mu)\), defines
  \[
  \mathrm{CP}(\overline s_\lambda\otimes\overline s_\mu)=
  \begin{cases}
  \overline{\Delta(s_\lambda)}-(\overline s_\lambda\otimes1),
     &\overline s_\mu=1,\\
  \overline{\Delta(s_\lambda)}(1\otimes\overline s_\mu),
     &\overline s_\mu\ne1,
  \end{cases}
  \tag{9}
  \]
  extended linearly on \(\overline\Lambda\otimes\overline\Lambda\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 373-397]
- [source-backed] Equation (10) is the update
  \[
  \xi^{(m)}=\xi^{(m-1)}
  -\gamma\,\mathrm{CP}\!\left(
  \overline s_\lambda\otimes
  (\overline s_{\mu^{(1)}}\cdots\overline s_{\mu^{(k)}})\right).
  \tag{10}
  \]
  The source then states that its only cancellation is the selected term and its negative in the subtracted \(\gamma\mathrm{CP}(\cdots)\), and concludes that update order does not affect the output. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 625-632]
- [source-backed] Definition 4.1 sets
  \[
  W=\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb Z}\{
  \operatorname{Lin}_\varphi(\rho):
  \rho\in\operatorname{Dec}_{\varphi}\text{ is wide}\}.
  \]
  Lemma 4.2 says that if \(N\le\min(j,n-r-i)\), then \(\operatorname{Lin}_\varphi(\nu)\in W\) for every tall \(\nu\). Lemma 4.3 supplies the scaled tuple \(\widehat\varphi=(4^qn,2^qr,i,2^qj,a,b,N)\) and its restriction property. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 738-789]
- [source-backed] **Theorem 4.4.** For every valid \(\varphi\), the system
  \[
  \left\{\operatorname{Lin}_\varphi(\nu)=d_\nu
  \mid\nu\in\operatorname{Dec}_{\varphi}\right\}
  \tag{13}
  \]
  is inconsistent if \(d_\nu=0\) for every wide \(\nu\) and \(d_\rho\ne0\) for some tall \(\rho\). Its proof first applies Lemma 4.2 when \(N\le\min(j,n-r-i)\); otherwise it chooses \(q\) with
  \[
  N\le\min(2^qj,\,4^qn-2^qr-i),
  \]
  defines \(e_\tau=d_\nu\) for \(\tau=\widehat\nu\) and \(e_\tau=0\) otherwise, and invokes Lemma 4.3. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 790-818]
- [source-backed] **Theorem 4.5.** For every valid \(\varphi\), no syzygy
  \[
  \sum_{\substack{\lambda\subseteq b^a\\|\lambda|=N}}
  \overline s_{(i^j,\lambda)}f_\lambda
  =
  \sum_{\substack{\lambda\subseteq b^a\\|\lambda|<N}}
  f_\lambda\overline s_{(i^j,\lambda)}
  \]
  exists with nonzero left side. The given proof cites Lemma 2.5 and Theorem 4.4. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 819-826]
